drivingQuestion: Why does R' Yehuda not disagree about a fish-like discharge as he does about a piece of tissue?
outcomeNote: the question is answered in the next unit (niddah.sugya099)

segments.he: הַמַּפֶּלֶת כְּמִין דָּגִים. וְלִיפְלוֹג נָמֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּהָא!
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: In the case of a woman «who discharges» an item «similar to fish» or to grasshoppers, repugnant creatures, or creeping animals, if blood emerges with it, the woman is impure, and if not, she is pure. The Gemara asks: «But let Rabbi Yehuda disagree» with the Rabbis «with regard to this» halakha «as well,» just as he disagrees with them in the first clause of the mishna, in the case where a woman discharges an amorphous piece of tissue, as he maintains that she is impure whether or not blood emerges with it.
